name: F-35 Lightning II
summary: The F-35 Lightning II is a 5th Generation multirole fighter combining advanced stealth, sensor fusion, network-enabled operations, and sustainment for the U.S. and partner nations.

name: F-22 Raptor
summary: The F-22 Raptor defines air dominance. Its combination of stealth, supercruise, agility, and integrated avionics enables lethal capability in contested airspace.

name: F-16 Fighting Falcon
summary: The F-16 Fighting Falcon is a versatile multirole fighter with more than 4,600 built, serving dozens of air forces worldwide with continuous modernization.

name: F-117 Nighthawk
summary: The F-117 Nighthawk was the world's first operational stealth aircraft. Its faceted design, born at Skunk Works, opened the era of low-observable combat aviation.

name: SR-71 Blackbird
summary: The SR-71 Blackbird remains the world's fastest and highest-flying air-breathing manned aircraft. Developed by Skunk Works, it could outrun surface-to-air missiles.

name: U-2 Dragon Lady
summary: The U-2 high-altitude reconnaissance aircraft, developed by Skunk Works, still provides critical intelligence, surveillance, and reconnaissance decades after its first flight.

name: F-104 Starfighter
summary: The Lockheed F-104 Starfighter — the 'missile with a man in it' — set speed and altitude records in the 1950s with its needle nose, tiny wings, and blistering climb performance.

name: C-130J Super Hercules
summary: The C-130J Super Hercules is the most advanced C-130 ever designed, built, and flown — the tactical airlifter of choice for more than 20 nations and dozens of operators.

name: C-5 Galaxy
summary: The C-5 Galaxy is one of the largest military transport aircraft in the world, moving outsized cargo and strategic lift for the U.S. Air Force across intercontinental ranges.

name: P-3 Orion
summary: The P-3 Orion maritime patrol aircraft has excelled for decades in anti-submarine warfare, surface surveillance, and search-and-rescue missions for navies worldwide.

name: L-1011 TriStar
summary: The L-1011 TriStar was a technologically advanced wide-body trijet airliner — often called one of the most sophisticated commercial aircraft of its era.

name: CH-53K King Stallion
summary: The CH-53K King Stallion is the most powerful helicopter in the U.S. military inventory, built by Sikorsky to lift extreme loads over long distances in high/hot conditions.

name: UH-60 Black Hawk
summary: The Sikorsky UH-60 Black Hawk is the world's most widely used multi-mission helicopter, with thousands in service for troop transport, MEDEVAC, and assault support.

name: Autonomous BLACK HAWK
summary: Lockheed Martin and DARPA demonstrated optionally piloted BLACK HAWK flight, showing how autonomy can extend logistics and resupply into contested battlefields.

name: Sikorsky S-92
summary: The Sikorsky S-92 serves military and civil missions — search and rescue, offshore transport, and VIP lift — with a strong safety and reliability record worldwide.

name: Presidential Helicopter (VH-92A)
summary: Sikorsky builds the VH-92A, the next-generation helicopter fleet for the President of the United States, combining security, communications, and reliable vertical lift.

name: HIMARS
summary: The M142 HIMARS is a highly mobile multiple rocket launcher on a wheeled chassis, delivering precision long-range fires for the U.S. Army and allied forces.

name: GMLRS
summary: Guided Multiple Launch Rocket System (GMLRS) rockets give HIMARS and MLRS units precision long-range fires, with extended-range variants expanding the engagement envelope.

name: ATACMS
summary: Army Tactical Missile System (ATACMS) is a surface-to-surface missile that delivers precision strikes against high-value targets at extended ranges from HIMARS and MLRS.

name: PrSM
summary: Precision Strike Missile (PrSM) is the next-generation surface-to-surface missile for HIMARS, offering greater range, lethality, and survivability than legacy ATACMS.

name: PAC-3 MSE
summary: The PAC-3 Missile Segment Enhancement (MSE) is a high-velocity hit-to-kill interceptor that extends the Patriot air-and-missile defense system's firepower and reach.

name: THAAD Weapon System
summary: Terminal High Altitude Area Defense (THAAD) is a combat-proven hit-to-kill system that intercepts short-, medium-, and intermediate-range ballistic missiles inside and outside the atmosphere.

name: Aegis Combat System
summary: The Aegis Combat System is the centralized command-and-control and weapons-control heart of the U.S. Navy surface fleet and allied Aegis ships worldwide.

name: Aegis Ashore
summary: Aegis Ashore extends naval Aegis missile-defense capability to land-based sites, protecting allies against ballistic missile threats with proven radar and interceptor software.

name: Javelin
summary: Javelin is a premier man-portable, fire-and-forget anti-tank missile — highly effective against modern tanks and light armored vehicles without exposing the gunner after launch.

name: Hellfire Missile
summary: The AGM-114 Hellfire is a combat-proven air-to-ground precision missile used from helicopters and fixed-wing platforms for anti-armor and precision strike missions.

name: LONGBOW Fire Control
summary: LONGBOW radar and fire control on the AH-64 Apache enable fire-and-forget targeting of multiple threats in all weather, day or night — shown here launching Hellfire.

name: AGM-179 JAGM
summary: The Joint Air-to-Ground Missile (JAGM) is a multi-mode precision strike missile replacing legacy systems for rotary- and fixed-wing platforms.

name: JASSM
summary: The Joint Air-to-Surface Standoff Missile (JASSM) is a long-range, low-observable cruise missile that lets aircraft strike defended targets from well outside enemy air defenses.

name: LRASM
summary: The Long Range Anti-Ship Missile (LRASM) is a precision-guided, intelligent anti-ship weapon designed for U.S. Navy and Air Force warfighters in contested maritime environments.

name: Hypersonic Strike Weapons
summary: Lockheed Martin develops hypersonic boost-glide and strike systems for rapid, long-range precision attack — shrinking the time from decision to effect against high-value targets.

name: Directed Energy Laser Systems
summary: Lockheed Martin's high-energy laser systems provide speed-of-light defense against drones, rockets, and other threats with precision and deep magazines.

name: Sniper Advanced Targeting Pod
summary: Sniper ATP is a combat-proven electro-optical targeting pod that gives fighters long-range identification, laser designation, and precision strike support day or night.

name: Trident II D5 Missile
summary: The Trident II D5 is a submarine-launched ballistic missile providing sea-based strategic nuclear deterrence for the U.S. Navy and the United Kingdom.

name: Polaris SLBM
summary: The UGM-27 Polaris was the first operational submarine-launched ballistic missile, revolutionizing strategic nuclear deterrence from the late 1950s onward.

name: Orion Spacecraft
summary: Lockheed Martin builds the Orion crew vehicle for NASA's Artemis program — designed to carry astronauts beyond low Earth orbit to the Moon and, eventually, Mars.

name: First Orion Test Flight (EFT-1)
summary: In 2014, Orion's Exploration Flight Test-1 successfully demonstrated high-speed reentry and recovery — a critical step toward crewed deep-space missions.

name: GPS III
summary: GPS III satellites, built by Lockheed Martin, deliver stronger, more accurate, and more jam-resistant global positioning signals for military and civil users worldwide.

name: SBIRS Satellite
summary: The Space-Based Infrared System (SBIRS) provides critical missile warning, missile defense, and battlespace awareness from geosynchronous and highly elliptical orbits.

name: Space Fence
summary: Space Fence is a ground-based radar system that tracks objects in Earth orbit, strengthening space situational awareness and collision avoidance for national security.

name: C2BMC
summary: Command, Control, Battle Management, and Communications (C2BMC) is the integrating 'brain' of the U.S. Ballistic Missile Defense System.

name: EADGE-T C2 Program
summary: EADGE-T (Enterprise Air Defense Ground Environment – Transformation) delivers an integrated command-and-control architecture for the UAE air and missile defense enterprise.

name: Founding of Skunk Works
summary: In 1943, Kelly Johnson founded Lockheed's Advanced Development Programs (Skunk Works) — a lean team that has since delivered many of the world's most advanced aircraft.

name: Have Blue Prototype
summary: In the late 1970s, the Have Blue demonstrator proved practical low-observable technology at Skunk Works — the direct ancestor of the F-117 Nighthawk.

name: First Flight of the U-2
summary: In 1955, the U-2 spy plane took its first flight, enabling high-altitude reconnaissance that shaped intelligence gathering throughout the Cold War.

name: First Flight of the F-117
summary: In 1981, the F-117 Nighthawk's first flight marked the dawn of operational stealth combat aviation.

name: Blackbird Mach 3+ Record
summary: In 1976, the SR-71 set absolute speed and altitude records for air-breathing manned aircraft — marks that still stand.

name: First Production F-35 Delivery
summary: In 2011, the first production F-35 was delivered, beginning the operational era of 5th-generation fighters for the U.S. and partner air forces.

name: Viking Mars Lander
summary: In 1976, the Viking 1 and 2 landers — built by Martin Marietta — became the first U.S. spacecraft to successfully land on Mars and return high-resolution surface images.

name: Viking 1 First Mars Photo
summary: In 1976, Viking 1 transmitted the first clear images from the Martian surface — a landmark in planetary exploration and Lockheed Martin heritage.

name: Apollo Program Contribution
summary: Heritage Lockheed and Martin companies contributed propulsion, systems, and hardware that helped put astronauts on the Moon during NASA's Apollo program.

name: The First Packed Parachute
summary: In 1913, Glenn L. Martin demonstrated a backpack-style packed parachute — a practical leap in aviation safety from one of Lockheed Martin's founding heritage companies.

name: Sinking of the Ostfriesland
summary: In 1921, Glenn Martin's MB-2 bombers helped prove that air power could sink capital ships when they struck the captured German battleship Ostfriesland.
